raw_response:
I have only 5 mu, so I will still do the wheat-maize rotation on all of it. That is the safest for my family. I have done this many years, and around here everybody does it this way. I cannot take big risks because cash is tight and some people in my house work outside, so field labor must be simple and on time. For wheat, I will sow in October after preparing the land, use an ordinary improved seed I can buy locally, put base fertilizer first, then add one topdressing if the seedlings and later the wheat color look weak. I have a well, so I will irrigate, but not too many times because pumping costs money. For maize, I will plant right after wheat harvest, very quickly, because that gap is short. I will keep the same 5 mu in maize, use hybrid seed like most neighbors, give enough fertilizer for a stable yield, and irrigate only if the rain is not enough. I would rather spend a little on fertilizer and water than lose too much yield, but I still keep it within what my family can afford.
